name: Pine bark extract
short: A systematic review of 27 small trials (1,641 participants) could draw no definitive conclusions about safety; most comparisons had no serious adverse event data. No interaction data were found.
text: A 2020 systematic review of 27 randomised trials (1,641 participants) of pine bark extract supplements across 10 chronic disorders found that, for most comparisons, studies did not report hospital admissions or serious adverse events, and concluded that no definitive conclusions about safety are possible because of small sample sizes, limited numbers of trials per condition, variation in outcome measures and poor reporting of the trials. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.

citations.label: Robertson et al., 2020, Cochrane Database Syst Rev
